source.title_or_context: Practical guidance on the use of diuretics in patients with heart failure

text_units.verbatim_text: Potentially all patients with symptoms and signs of congestion, irrespective of LVEF.

normative_assertions.notes: Agent-silver extraction preserves explicit source wording and inherited table context; human adjudication remains required.

text_units.verbatim_text: When used, should always be used in a combination with an ACE-I (or an ARB), a beta-blocker, and an MRA in patients with HFrEF (unless any of these drugs is not tolerated/contraindicated), until signs of congestion have been relieved.

normative_assertions.notes: Agent-silver extraction preserves explicit source wording and inherited table context; human adjudication remains required.

text_units.verbatim_text: Thiazide diuretics can be used in patients with preserved renal function and mild symptoms of congestion. However, the majority of patients require loop diuretics (or combined with a thiazide diuretic and an MRA) due to the severity of HF symptoms and steadily deteriorating kidney function.

normative_assertions.notes: Agent-silver extraction preserves explicit source wording and inherited table context; human adjudication remains required.

text_units.verbatim_text: Not indicated if the patient has never had symptoms or signs of congestion.

normative_assertions.notes: Agent-silver extraction preserves explicit source wording and inherited table context; human adjudication remains required.

text_units.verbatim_text: Known allergic reaction/other adverse reaction (drug-specific).

normative_assertions.notes: Agent-silver extraction preserves explicit source wording and inherited table context; human adjudication remains required.

text_units.verbatim_text: Significant hypokalaemia ( $K^+ \leq 3.5$ mmol/L)—may be made worse by diuretic.

normative_assertions.notes: Agent-silver extraction preserves explicit source wording and inherited table context; human adjudication remains required.

text_units.verbatim_text: Significant renal dysfunction [creatinine $>221$ $\mu$ mol/L ( $>2.5$ mg/dL) or eGFR $<30$ mL/min/1.73 m2]a—may be made worse by diuretic or patient may not respond to diuretic (especially thiazide diuretic).

normative_assertions.notes: Agent-silver extraction preserves explicit source wording and inherited table context; human adjudication remains required.

text_units.verbatim_text: Symptomatic or severe asymptomatic hypotension (SBP $<90$ mmHg)—may be made worse by diuretic-induced hypovolaemia.

normative_assertions.notes: Descriptive/contextual source text; no normative action is inferred.

text_units.verbatim_text: Drug interactions to look out for:

normative_assertions.notes: Descriptive/contextual source text; no normative action is inferred.

text_units.verbatim_text: Combination with an ACE-I, an ARB, or a renin inhibitora—risk of hypotension (usually not a problem).

normative_assertions.notes: Descriptive/contextual source text; no normative action is inferred.

text_units.verbatim_text: Combination with other diuretics (e.g. loop plus thiazide)—risk of hypovolaemia, hypotension, hypokalaemia, and renal impairmentb.

normative_assertions.notes: Descriptive/contextual source text; no normative action is inferred.

text_units.verbatim_text: NSAIDsc—may attenuate effect of diuretic.

header_path: *WHICH DIURETIC AND WHAT DAILY DOSE?Loop diuretics:

normative_assertions.notes: Agent-silver extraction preserves explicit source wording and inherited table context; human adjudication remains required.

text_units.verbatim_text: Furosemide: starting dose 20–40 mg, usual dose 40–240 mg.

header_path: *WHICH DIURETIC AND WHAT DAILY DOSE?Loop diuretics:

normative_assertions.notes: Agent-silver extraction preserves explicit source wording and inherited table context; human adjudication remains required.

text_units.verbatim_text: Bumetanide: starting dose 0.5–1 mg, usual dose 1–5 mg.

header_path: *WHICH DIURETIC AND WHAT DAILY DOSE?Loop diuretics:

text_units.verbatim_text: Torasemide: starting dose 5–10 mg, usual dose 10–20 mg.

normative_assertions.notes: Agent-silver extraction preserves explicit source wording and inherited table context; human adjudication remains required.

text_units.verbatim_text: Bendroflumethiazide: starting dose 2.5 mg, usual dose 2.5–10 mg.

normative_assertions.notes: Agent-silver extraction preserves explicit source wording and inherited table context; human adjudication remains required.

text_units.verbatim_text: Hydrochlorothiazide: starting dose 25 mg, usual dose 12.5–100 mg.

normative_assertions.notes: Agent-silver extraction preserves explicit source wording and inherited table context; human adjudication remains required.

text_units.verbatim_text: Metolazone: starting dose 2.5 mg, usual dose 2.5–10 mg. Can be weekly, daily, or prn.

normative_assertions.notes: Agent-silver extraction preserves explicit source wording and inherited table context; human adjudication remains required.

text_units.verbatim_text: Indapamide: starting dose 2.5 mg, usual dose 2.5–5 mg.

normative_assertions.notes: Agent-silver extraction preserves explicit source wording and inherited table context; human adjudication remains required.

text_units.verbatim_text: Check renal function and electrolytes, particularly in those on a combination of loop and thiazide diuretics.

normative_assertions.notes: Agent-silver extraction preserves explicit source wording and inherited table context; human adjudication remains required.

text_units.verbatim_text: Start with a low dose but target an effective dose for a patient to achieve positive diuresis with a simultaneous reduction of body weight by 0.75–1.0 kg per day.

normative_assertions.notes: Agent-silver extraction preserves explicit source wording and inherited table context; human adjudication remains required.

text_units.verbatim_text: Adjust a dose according to symptoms and/or signs of congestion, blood pressure, and renal function. Use a minimum dose necessary to maintain euvolaemia—the patient's 'dry weight' (i.e. to keep the patient free of symptoms and signs of congestion).

normative_assertions.notes: Agent-silver extraction preserves explicit source wording and inherited table context; human adjudication remains required.

text_units.verbatim_text: Dose may need to be increased or decreased according to the patient's volume status (remember that excessive diuresis is more dangerous than oedema itself).

normative_assertions.notes: Agent-silver extraction preserves explicit source wording and inherited table context; human adjudication remains required.

text_units.verbatim_text: Re-check blood chemistry 1–2 weeks after an initiation and after any increase in dose (urea/BUN, creatinine, K+).

normative_assertions.notes: Agent-silver extraction preserves explicit source wording and inherited table context; human adjudication remains required.

text_units.verbatim_text: When to stop uptitration, reduce dose, stop treatment—see PROBLEM SOLVING.

normative_assertions.notes: Agent-silver extraction preserves explicit source wording and inherited table context; human adjudication remains required.

text_units.verbatim_text: Patients can be educated to alter their own diuretic dose, according to need (based on symptoms, signs, and weight changes).

text_units.verbatim_text: A specialist HF nurse may assist with education of the patient, follow-up (in person or by telephone), biochemical monitoring, and dose adjustment (including patient educated in dose adjustment).
